head: claude/mi165-be-floor-sweep-20260907
title: MI-165: the path-aware be_floor_r sweep — no value clears the gate
body:
**Tier-1 · PROPOSE-ONLY · `landing: "hold"`** (see `.github/pr-landing/mi165-be-floor-sweep-20260907.json`)

Closes the gap MI-163 (#11259) explicitly left open. `be_floor_r` is declared in **no config and armed on no leg**; arming it is Tier-3 and **the recommendation is not to arm it at any value.**

## The question

MI-163 measured that 36 of 44 enabled+live legs run a monotone Chandelier ratchet calibrated far beyond where trades go — median `R_TO_BREAKEVEN` (`trail_mult / atr_stop_mult`) **2.00R** against a median live peak of **0.84R**, so the stop reached break-even on 14 of 89 (15.7%) and banked +1R on 4 of 89 (4.5%). It produced a **gross** benefit table peaking at **+16.87R at +0.75R** and correctly **refused to propose a value**: the live telemetry carries `peak_r`, `open_r` and `giveback_r` and **no intra-trade path**, so the *forgone continuation* — what a trade that retraced to X and then **resumed** would have paid — is unmeasurable from it.

A bar-replay harness records the exit the floor actually causes, so that cost is **measured by construction, not estimated**.

*(MI-163's arithmetic was re-verified here, not carried over: resolving all 44 legs through `pipeline.monitor_unit_for` reproduces 19 donchian + 16 pullback + 1 squeeze = 36 ratchet legs, 8 `ict_scalp`, and `trail_mult/atr_stop_mult` spanning 1.20–3.33, median 2.00. Every figure matches.)*

## The result — no arm clears the gate

**POPULATION: 28 graded ratchet legs, 4090 control trades, BACKTEST.** ⚠️ Never poolable with MI-163's 89 **live** telemetry rows — those are precisely what cannot be replayed.

| `be_floor_r` | net total R | Δ vs control | legs better/worse/inert | GATE |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| **0.0 (control)** | **+671.58** | — | — | — |
| 0.50 | +526.42 | **−145.16** | 9 / 19 / 0 | FAIL |
| **0.75** | +543.45 | **−128.13** | 8 / 20 / 0 | FAIL |
| 1.00 | +572.50 | **−99.08** | 10 / 18 / 0 | FAIL |
| 1.50 | +636.54 | **−35.04** | 11 / 12 / 5 | FAIL |

Every arm loses, **monotonically in the floor** — the signature of forgone continuation. +0.75R, the peak of the gross table, is the second-worst arm tested. The benefit MI-163 measured is real (8–11 legs improve at every arm) but is swamped by trades that retraced through entry and then resumed.

## ⚠️ The finding that outlives this lever

**`be_floor_r = 1.5` wins a strict majority of exercised folds under ALL THREE fold-panel members and still loses 35R.**

| arm | k=3 | k=4 | k=5 | majority-win under all k? |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1.50 | 34W/25L/**25 inert** | 42W/29L/**41 inert** | 56W/30L/**54 inert** | **YES** |

A gate written as "majority of folds positive" would have passed it, because 30–39% of its folds are **inert** — the lever never fired. Its wins are many small fold-level improvements; its losses are a few very large truncated winners, which fold-counting cannot see. This is `BL-20260817-FLEET-SWEEP-WF-COUNTS-INERT-FOLDS-AS-WINS` reproducing on live-fleet parameters, and it is why the gate requires pooled-net **AND** fold-majority. (`1.0` at k=5 shows the milder version: 67W/66L against −99.08R pooled — the *fixed* panel catches it; a caller-chosen `--folds 5` would not.)

## What lands

- **`be_floor_r` in all three ratchet harnesses** (`backtest_trend` / `backtest_pullback` / `backtest_squeeze` — the three units share one trail geometry, so a lever meaning different things in each would make the pooled number incomparable). `max()`-ed against the chandelier candidate so it can **only ever tighten**, preserving the monotone-ratchet invariant. **Default `0.0` is byte-identical**, verified against `HEAD` for all three before any arm was run.
- **`scripts/research/be_floor_sweep.py`** — arms, a **fixed** fold panel `{3,4,5}` (`BL-20260730-WF-FOLDCOUNT-VERDICT-FLIP`), calendar folds (five arms need a *common* partition), and inertness **imported** from `m20_wf_effective.is_inert` rather than restated.
- **Tests** pinning no-op-at-default in all three harnesses, the only-ever-tightens invariant (asserted per-trade, not on an aggregate), and **the forgone continuation itself** on a hand-built path. `be_floor_r` registered in `test_trend_harness_levers`' `ALL_LEVERS_AT_DEFAULT`, whose own comment says a lever absent from it is a lever nothing pins.
- **The memo** (`docs/research/be-floor-sweep-2026-09-07.md`) + the full per-leg/per-fold JSON record, and **two backlog rows**.

## Stated bounds

- **7 legs `insufficient_n`** (all `*_trend_long_1d`, n = 21–29 vs the repo's floor of 30) and **1 `degenerate_series`** (`splg_trend_long_1d` — Yahoo served 36 bars with **1 usable close**; graded by the repo's own `candle_variance.grade_close_variance`). That state is kept **apart from `insufficient_n` deliberately**: *we could not look* is not *a leg that traded too little*.
- **The 8 `ict_scalp` legs are out of scope by construction** — their one-shot `monitor_breakeven_sl` is guarded by `sl < entry`, so it fires once and cannot accrue R. A break-even *floor* is meaningless on a mechanism whose ceiling is already break-even. MI-164's hook changes what can be *measured* about them, not whether this lever applies.
- **MES/MGC/MHG are replayed on `ES=F`/`GC=F`/`HG=F`** continuous front-month proxies — the repo's own mapping (`yf_symbols.py`), but an approximation. Two of the three are `insufficient_n` anyway.
- **`--source yfinance` could not be used**: the library's `fc.yahoo.com` cookie handshake is reset by this session's proxy, so every call fails at the COOKIE stage and reports *"no candles returned"* — a message naming a fetch that never happened. Yahoo's chart endpoint answers normally. Filed as `BL-20260907-YFINANCE-LANE-BLOCKED-BY-PROXY-COOKIE-HANDSHAKE`.
- **No value above 1.5R was tested** and none is endorsed by extrapolation — a floor that arms almost never converges on *doing nothing*, and 38.6% of folds are already inert at 1.5R.
- Fidelity: across all 36 legs the number of declared config levers the matching harness could **not** model is **zero** (measured — the sweep filters against each harness's real signature and reports drops).

## Why `landing: "hold"`

R5 refuses self-land because three changed paths (`scripts/backtest_{trend,pullback,squeeze}.py`) sit outside `TIER1_SURFACE`, which covers `scripts/ci|ops|research|reports` but not the backtest harnesses at `scripts/` root — correctly, and not as a danger claim. **None of the five `HOLD_REASONS` names "Tier-1 work the guard cannot certify"**, so the declaration states the closest term and puts the true cause in `hold_text`. Filed as `BL-20260907-PR-LANDING-HAS-NO-HOLD-REASON-FOR-TIER1-WORK-OUTSIDE-THE-CERTIFIABLE-SURFACE`; not fixed here because both candidate fixes edit `check_pr_landing.py`, which is `LANDING_MACHINERY`, and R12 would bar this PR from landing its own fix. Auto-merge is deliberately **not** armed (R10).

## Verification

`run_guards.py --base main`: **PASS 71 · FAIL 1 · SKIP 18** — the one failure was `layer-guard` exiting **127** (`lint-imports` not installed in this sandbox); installed and re-ran it: **6 contracts kept, 0 broken**. `ruff check .` clean. 46 lever tests pass. *(45 test modules cannot collect here for want of `fastapi`, identically on `origin/main` — environmental, not this change.)*
